data.comparison: Round 2 executed four new shared schedules, all 25/25 valid: G1 [9,5,5,5] condition 0.802095 Å / gap 3.651607 pIC50; G2 [7,7,5,5] 0.795613 / 3.626030; G3 [7,5,5,3] 0.795696 / 3.626080; G4 [3,3,5,7] 0.793734 / 3.627947. Nine shared schedules are now executed. Condition order: [3,3,5,7] 0.793734 < [5,5,5,7] 0.794247 < [3,5,5,5] 0.794287 < [5,5,5,5] 0.794651 < [5,5,5,3] 0.795071 < [7,5,5,5] 0.795294 < [7,7,5,5] 0.795613 < [7,5,5,3] 0.795696 < [9,5,5,5] 0.802095. Functional gap order: [7,7,5,5] 3.626030 < [7,5,5,3] 3.626080 < [7,5,5,5] 3.626228 < [3,5,5,5] 3.627548 < [5,5,5,3] 3.627612 < [5,5,5,5] 3.627717 < [5,5,5,7] 3.627840 < [3,3,5,7] 3.627947 < [9,5,5,5] 3.651607. The 0.02 Å band anchored at 0.793734 contains all nine means, with 0.0116 Å of margin at the worst schedule, so condition does not separate any of them; inside the band the functional gap is the only discriminator, and excluding the 9 anchor that spread is just 0.001917 pIC50. One real effect was found this round: the interval0=9 overshoot penalises both means (+0.006802 Å and +0.025379 pIC50 versus [7,5,5,5], paired G1-vs-G2 mean affinity disadvantage 0.025577 at win rate 0.48) while raising only the single best candidate to 7.215729. The joint early reduction [3,3,5,7] moved the condition frontier 0.000513 Å below [5,5,5,7] at a 0.000107 pIC50 gap cost, so early-amplitude reduction is currently the only direction buying condition, and it remains a joint (interval0 + interval1) change that no executed schedule isolates. Interval3 stays a ≤0.0004 Å compensator. Best pIC50 remains 7.215729, i.e. −0.62210 below teacher 7.837829; no schedule exceeds teacher. Dedup: G1:H1 ticks [7,7,5,5] are identical to the executed r02:G2 anchor, so running it would reproduce known numbers (0.795613 / 3.626030) rather than add independent evidence.
data.failure_directions: (1) Upward interval0 extension beyond 7 is now a demonstrated mean failure: [9,5,5,5] is worst on both means and carries a 0.025577 pIC50 mean affinity disadvantage against [7,7,5,5]; therefore G2:H1 [9,7,5,5] and G2:H2 [9,9,5,5] repeat a known failure in a new background and are ranked last but one and last but two. Keep 9 only as a best-bonus reference. (2) Interval3 amplitude as a standalone lever is exhausted: 3-5-7 differ by at most 0.000404 Å condition and 0.000148 pIC50 ([5,5,5,7] 0.794247 vs [5,5,5,5] 0.794651; [7,5,5,3] 0.795696 vs [7,5,5,5] 0.795294), so no slot should be spent on it alone; it is carried only as background. (3) Fine interpolation of a sub-tolerance edge has low decision value: G3:H1 [6,5,5,5] largely re-describes the [5,5,5,5]→[7,5,5,5] curve whose endpoints differ by 0.000643 Å, and it also changes interval3, so a gain would be confounded. (4) Duplicate execution is not evidence: G1:H1 [7,7,5,5] equals the executed G2 anchor and is ranked last. (5) Best-affinity-only reasoning must not steer allocation: the highest single candidate (7.215729 at [9,5,5,5]) came with the worst group means on both axes.

data.public_memory: Version v8 teacher memory after round 2. Condition frontier: [3,3,5,7] mean RMSD 0.793734 Å. Functional frontier: [7,7,5,5] mean affinity gap 3.626030 pIC50 ([7,5,5,3] 3.626080; [7,5,5,5] 3.626228). Best pIC50 7.215729 at [9,5,5,5], −0.62210 versus teacher 7.837829; no schedule exceeds teacher. The 0.02 Å band anchored at 0.793734 contains all nine executed means (worst 0.802095, 0.0116 Å margin), so condition cannot rank them; inside the band the functional gap discriminates and, excluding the 9 anchor, spans only 0.001917 pIC50. Response: interval0 is curved. 5→7 cost 0.000643 Å and gained 0.001489 pIC50; 7→9 cost 0.006802 Å and 0.025379 pIC50 while raising only the single best candidate — keep interval0 ≤ 7. Interval1 5→7 at interval0=7 gave +0.000319 Å and −0.000198 pIC50, a weak function-favouring move that nonetheless produced the pool's lowest gap. Joint early reduction 5,5→3,3 with interval3=7 lowered the mean 0.000513 Å at 0.000107 pIC50 gap cost; label it joint, since interval0 and interval1 are not isolated. Interval3 is a ≤0.0004 Å compensator, not a lever. Background: condition and function are near-tied across early amplitudes 3–7, so a schedule only counts as an improvement if it moves one axis by roughly 0.002 or more without paying on the other. Alternative: if [1,3,5,7] and [3,1,5,7] are both flat, early amplitude is exhausted and interval2 — never varied in any executed schedule — is the last untested interval; if interval1 reduction at [7,3,5,5] or [7,3,5,3] lowers condition without gap loss, that background replaces [7,7,5,5] as the shared incumbent. Falsifier: neither early-isolation probe falls below 0.793734 Å, or any condition gain costs more than 0.005 pIC50 of gap. Next action: run [1,3,5,7] and [3,1,5,7] as the interval0/interval1 isolation pair, and [7,3,5,5] with [7,3,5,3] to close the interval1 bracket at the functional frontier, reading each delta against its matched executed anchor rather than against a selected incumbent. Dedup: [7,7,5,5] is already executed as the r02:G2 anchor, so G1:H1 is a re-measurement, not independent evidence.
